definition: the hope that lifting the load would give her the need-meeting, and where it landed

settled:
For most of the marriage Jen held that the stress was what was withholding me, and that lifting it would give back the man and the need-meeting with him.

Retirement lifted it. I am much better on that dimension and still not meeting those needs, and she has become deeply discouraged.

The needs were never deferred by load. What she wants is attachment-love, and that is structurally unavailable rather than recoverable.

Every rise in my capacity that does not produce it is further evidence that capacity was never the bottleneck.

Whether my care lands depends on her being able to believe what she needs to. That is the one capacity she has and I do not.

On 6 August 2026 I downgraded that claim. I think it is no longer load-bearing as it was: still fraught, but no longer deadly to break silence. The conditional landing is a cost I pay rather than the condition the marriage rests on.

title: What Recovery Did Not Give Her
